accepted.s: The Look East Policy of India was launched during which period under which Prime Minister?
accepted.x: The Look East Policy was launched in the early 1990s, specifically 1991–92, during the tenure of Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.
accepted.tq: Use the date-and-person combination to distinguish the policy from its later upgrade.
accepted.sec: Look East to Act East - origin, launch and upgrade, 3C/4C, North-East gateway, ASEAN connectivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the original primary focus of India's Look East Policy?
o: Trade, investment and the ASEAN Free Trade Area
Energy cooperation with the Gulf countries
accepted.x: The Look East Policy originally had an economic focus centred on trade, investment and the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AIFTA).
accepted.tq: Identify the original economic orientation before considering the later strategic expansion.
accepted.sec: Look East to Act East - origin, launch and upgrade, 3C/4C, North-East gateway, ASEAN connectivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Act East Policy was formally launched in 2014 at which of the following forums and under whose leadership?
o: SAARC Summit in Nepal, under Narendra Modi
BIMSTEC Summit in Thailand, under Atal Bihari Vajpayee
East Asia Summit in Myanmar, under Narendra Modi
accepted.x: The Act East Policy was launched in 2014 at the East Asia Summit held in Myanmar during the prime ministership of Narendra Modi.
accepted.tq: Match the launch year, forum and political leadership.
accepted.sec: Look East to Act East - origin, launch and upgrade, 3C/4C, North-East gateway, ASEAN connectivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Act East Policy:
1. It was initially conceived as an economic policy.
2. It was later extended to political, strategic and cultural fields.
3. It is limited to East Asia and excludes the wider Indo-Pacific.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the Act East Policy has a wider Indo-Pacific orientation.
accepted.tq: Separate the policy's economic origin from its later strategic and geographical expansion.
accepted.sec: Look East to Act East - origin, launch and upgrade, 3C/4C, North-East gateway, ASEAN connectivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 3Cs associated with India's Act East Policy are:
accepted.x: The 3Cs are Commerce, Culture and Connectivity. The 4C formulation adds Capacity Building.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of a compact policy acronym.
accepted.sec: Look East to Act East - origin, launch and upgrade, 3C/4C, North-East gateway, ASEAN connectivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is added to the 3Cs to form the 4C formulation of the Act East Policy?
accepted.x: Capacity building is the additional C in the 4C formulation: Commerce, Culture, Connectivity and Capacity Building.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related policy terms beginning with the same letter.
accepted.sec: Look East to Act East - origin, launch and upgrade, 3C/4C, North-East gateway, ASEAN connectivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly explains the role of India's North-Eastern region in the Act East framework?
o: It is outside the geographical scope of the Act East Policy.
It is regarded as India's gateway to the Gulf region.
It is regarded as India's gateway to ASEAN.
It is treated exclusively as a maritime gateway to Africa.
accepted.x: India's North-Eastern region is regarded as the gateway to ASEAN and is central to land connectivity with Southeast Asia.
accepted.tq: Apply the geographical metaphor of a policy to identify the relevant region.
accepted.sec: Look East to Act East - origin, launch and upgrade, 3C/4C, North-East gateway, ASEAN connectivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following have been identified as drivers of India's Look East Policy?
1. Countering China's influence
2. Access to new markets
3. Instability in West and Central Asia
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three factors—countering China, seeking new markets and instability in West and Central Asia—were identified as drivers of the Look East Policy.
accepted.tq: Test whether the candidate can combine strategic, economic and regional-security drivers.
accepted.sec: Look East to Act East - origin, launch and upgrade, 3C/4C, North-East gateway, ASEAN connectivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to ASEAN connectivity, consider the following projects:
1. Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project
2. India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway
3. Akhaura-Agartala railway link
Which of the projects given above are ASEAN-linked projects?
accepted.x: The Kaladan Multi-Modal Project and India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway are ASEAN-linked connectivity projects. The Akhaura-Agartala rail link is associated with Bangladesh.
accepted.tq: Use the country-partnership distinction to eliminate the project linked with Bangladesh.
accepted.sec: Look East to Act East - origin, launch and upgrade, 3C/4C, North-East gateway, ASEAN connectivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to recent upgrades in India's Act East partnerships?
accepted.x: Malaysia's Comprehensive Strategic Partnership dates to 2024, and the Philippines became a strategic partner in August 2025. The Vietnam entry is not the specified upgrade in this context.
accepted.tq: Check the year and type of partnership before accepting a country-policy pairing.
accepted.sec: Look East to Act East - origin, launch and upgrade, 3C/4C, North-East gateway, ASEAN connectivity  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India's Connect Central Asia policy was announced in 2012 at:
accepted.x: India announced the Connect Central Asia policy in 2012 at Bishkek.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the launch venue from later dialogue venues in Central Asia.
accepted.sec: Connect Central Asia policy - India-Central Asia Dialogue, Summit, Chabahar  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first India-Central Asia Dialogue of foreign ministers was hosted by which country and held at which city?
accepted.x: Uzbekistan hosted the first India-Central Asia Dialogue at Samarkand in 2019. Afghanistan was also invited.
accepted.tq: Pair the host country with the city rather than confusing it with the policy-launch venue.
accepted.sec: Connect Central Asia policy - India-Central Asia Dialogue, Summit, Chabahar  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the first India-Central Asia Dialogue is correct?
o: It was organised by Afghanistan with Pakistan as an invitee.
It was held in 2022 as a virtual summit.
It was organised by India without any invited partner.
Uzbekistan organised it and Afghanistan was invited.
accepted.x: The first Dialogue was organised by Uzbekistan at Samarkand in 2019, and Afghanistan was invited.
accepted.tq: Use the organiser-and-invitee combination to reject swapped institutional roles.
accepted.sec: Connect Central Asia policy - India-Central Asia Dialogue, Summit, Chabahar  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The first India-Central Asia Summit was held in:
accepted.x: The first India-Central Asia Summit was held virtually in January 2022.
accepted.tq: Combine the year with the mode of meeting to distinguish the Summit from the earlier Dialogue.
accepted.sec: Connect Central Asia policy - India-Central Asia Dialogue, Summit, Chabahar  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the five Central Asian states that sent delegations to India in 2025?
accepted.x: The five states were Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Azerbaijan is not included in this five-state grouping.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a fixed regional list.
accepted.sec: Connect Central Asia policy - India-Central Asia Dialogue, Summit, Chabahar  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following developments describes the India-Uzbekistan relationship in August 2026?
o: It was reduced to a strategic partnership with a $1 billion trade target by 2028.
It was raised to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, with a $5 billion trade target by 2030 and a uranium-supply framework.
It was converted into a defence alliance with a $10 billion trade target by 2030.
It was limited to cultural cooperation without an economic target.
accepted.x: In August 2026, India-Uzbekistan ties were raised to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, with a $5 billion trade target by 2030 and a framework for uranium supply.
accepted.tq: Read the complete development as a partnership-status, target-year and sectoral package.
accepted.sec: Connect Central Asia policy - India-Central Asia Dialogue, Summit, Chabahar  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Chabahar Port is strategically important to India primarily because it:
o: provides the shortest route to Southeast Asia through Myanmar
connects India directly to the European Union without passing through Iran
provides a route to Afghanistan, Central Asia and the INSTC while bypassing Pakistan
is India's principal naval base in the Bay of Bengal
accepted.x: Located in Iran on the Gulf of Oman, Chabahar provides access to Afghanistan, Central Asia and the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC), bypassing Pakistan.
accepted.tq: Identify the strategic value by linking location, destination and bypass route.
accepted.sec: Connect Central Asia policy - India-Central Asia Dialogue, Summit, Chabahar  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which recent development affected India's position regarding sanctions related to Chabahar?
o: Iran transferred Chabahar to India without conditions.
The INSTC was formally withdrawn from the Chabahar route.
The United States extended India's permanent exemption from all sanctions.
The United States ended India's Chabahar sanctions waiver.
accepted.x: The United States ended India's sanctions waiver for Chabahar, affecting the operating environment around the port.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of a policy change—ending a waiver rather than granting one.
accepted.sec: Connect Central Asia policy - India-Central Asia Dialogue, Summit, Chabahar  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Neighbourhood First policy was launched in 2014, as symbolised by:
o: inviting SAARC leaders to the Prime Minister's swearing-in ceremony in May 2014
inviting BIMSTEC leaders to the 2014 swearing-in ceremony
holding the first India-Central Asia Summit in 2014
accepted.x: The policy was associated with inviting SAARC leaders to the Prime Minister's swearing-in ceremony in May 2014. BIMSTEC leaders were invited in 2019.
accepted.tq: Use the year and regional grouping together to distinguish SAARC from BIMSTEC.
accepted.sec: Neighbourhood First policy - launch, principles, assistance

accepted.s: Which regional grouping's leaders were invited to the Indian Prime Minister's event in 2019 in the context of Neighbourhood First?
accepted.x: BIMSTEC leaders were invited in 2019, following the earlier invitation to SAARC leaders in 2014.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between neighbouring regional organisations by the year of invitation.
accepted.sec: Neighbourhood First policy - launch, principles, assistance

accepted.s:
The Neighbourhood First policy aims to promote which forms of connectivity across South Asia?
1. Physical connectivity
2. Digital connectivity
3. People-to-people connectivity
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The policy seeks physical, digital and people-to-people connectivity across South Asia.
accepted.tq: Recognise the three complementary dimensions of regional connectivity.
accepted.sec: Neighbourhood First policy - launch, principles, assistance

accepted.s: Which of the following principles is associated with the Gujral Doctrine and forms part of the roots of Neighbourhood First?
o: Strict reciprocity in every bilateral agreement
Non-reciprocity, non-interference and no territory being used against a neighbour
Non-interference only, without any territorial principle
accepted.x: The Gujral Doctrine emphasised non-reciprocity, non-interference and ensuring that a country's territory is not used against a neighbour.
accepted.tq: Select the complete set of principles rather than a partial or reversed formulation.
accepted.sec: Neighbourhood First policy - launch, principles, assistance

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of India's assistance or connectivity initiatives under Neighbourhood First?
o: A Gulf Cooperation Council customs union
accepted.x: COVID-19 vaccine assistance, Bhutan hydropower, and Sri Lanka rooftop solar projects are examples associated with Neighbourhood First. A GCC customs union is not such an initiative.
accepted.tq: Identify the regional outsider among examples of neighbourhood assistance.
accepted.sec: Neighbourhood First policy - launch, principles, assistance

accepted.s: The Link West policy primarily seeks to deepen India's relations with:
o: Only the countries of South Asia
Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific Islands
Central Asia, Japan and South Korea
accepted.x: Link West, also called Think West, focuses on the Gulf, Iran and Israel.
accepted.tq: Match the policy label with its westward geographical focus.
accepted.sec: Link West / Think West - Gulf, Iran, Israel, I2U2

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a major objective of India's Link West policy?
accepted.x: Energy, trade, diaspora and counter-terrorism are all objectives associated with Link West. Therefore, none of the listed choices is actually outside the policy; the question is invalid as framed.
accepted.tq: Check every option against the complete objective list before selecting an exception.
accepted.sec: Link West / Think West - Gulf, Iran, Israel, I2U2

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India's relationship with the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region as stated in the policy context?
o: About $16 billion in trade and 1 million members of the diaspora
Over $500 billion in trade and 50 million members of the diaspora
No significant trade or diaspora relationship
Over $160 billion in trade and about 10 million members of the Indian diaspora
accepted.x: The GCC region accounts for over $160 billion in trade with India and around 10 million members of the Indian diaspora, making it India's largest socio-economic partner in this context.
accepted.tq: Retain the paired trade-and-diaspora figures rather than treating them as separate facts.
accepted.sec: Link West / Think West - Gulf, Iran, Israel, I2U2

accepted.s: As stated in the relevant policy context, how many visits had Prime Minister Modi made to GCC states and how many to Israel?
o: 15 to GCC states and 2 to Israel
20 to GCC states and 2 to Israel
10 to GCC states and 1 to Israel
15 to GCC states and 5 to Israel
accepted.x: The figures given are 15 visits to GCC states and two visits to Israel.
accepted.tq: Compare the two close numerical figures in the same diplomatic context.
accepted.sec: Link West / Think West - Gulf, Iran, Israel, I2U2

accepted.s: The I2U2 grouping consists of:
o: India, Israel, UAE and the United States
India, Israel, Ukraine and the United States
India, Indonesia, UAE and the United States
India, Iran, UAE and the United Kingdom
accepted.x: I2U2 comprises India, Israel, the United Arab Emirates and the United States, and is also called the West Asia Quad.
accepted.tq: Expand each initial carefully and reject look-alike country names.
accepted.sec: Link West / Think West - Gulf, Iran, Israel, I2U2

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding I2U2:
1. It is also known as the West Asia Quad.
2. Its first leaders' summit was held virtually in 2022.
3. The Economic Diplomacy Division of the Ministry of External Affairs handles it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: I2U2 is the West Asia Quad, its first leaders' summit was virtual in 2022, and it is handled by the MEA's Economic Diplomacy Division.
accepted.tq: Combine the grouping's name, summit format and responsible institutional division.
accepted.sec: Link West / Think West - Gulf, Iran, Israel, I2U2

accepted.s: SAGAR, announced in 2015 at Mauritius, stands for:
o: Sustainable Advancement and Growth across Regions
Strategic Alliance for Global Action and Resilience
Security and Governance across Regional Seas
Security and Growth for All in the Region
accepted.x: SAGAR stands for Security and Growth for All in the Region and was announced in Mauritius in 2015.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of the maritime vision along with its launch context.
accepted.sec: SAGAR doctrine - announcement, MAHASAGAR, SHANTI

accepted.s:
Which of the following correctly matches the maritime vision with its year and full form?
1. SAGAR — 2015 — Security and Growth for All in the Region
2. MAHASAGAR — 2025 — Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
3. SHANTI — 13 July 2026 — Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All three matches are correct. SAGAR and MAHASAGAR were announced in Mauritius in 2015 and 2025 respectively, while SHANTI was announced on 13 July 2026 by EAM Jaishankar.
accepted.tq: Verify each acronym against both its date and its expanded form.
accepted.sec: SAGAR doctrine - announcement, MAHASAGAR, SHANTI

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes India's SAGAR doctrine?
o: A trade-only framework excluding security concerns
India as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region, including a response to China's String of Pearls
India's withdrawal from maritime security affairs in the Indian Ocean Region
A continental security arrangement limited to Central Asia
accepted.x: SAGAR presents India as a net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region and is associated with countering China's String of Pearls strategy.
accepted.tq: Infer the doctrine's strategic meaning from its security-provider role and regional setting.
accepted.sec: SAGAR doctrine - announcement, MAHASAGAR, SHANTI

accepted.s: SHANTI is intended to serve as:
o: A replacement for the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative
A normative framework for shared maritime spaces, first to be operationalised in the Bay of Bengal
A trade agreement among Central Asian states
A military alliance for exclusive naval operations
accepted.x: SHANTI is a normative framework for shared maritime spaces and is to be operationalised first in the Bay of Bengal.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a normative maritime framework from an alliance or trade agreement.
accepted.sec: SAGAR doctrine - announcement, MAHASAGAR, SHANTI

accepted.s: India's free, open and inclusive Indo-Pacific vision, with ASEAN centrality, was set out by Prime Minister Modi in the keynote address at the Shangri-La Dialogue in:
accepted.x: Prime Minister Modi set out this vision in his Shangri-La Dialogue keynote in June 2018.
accepted.tq: Link the speech, year and core phrase of the Indo-Pacific vision.
accepted.sec: Indo-Pacific vision - Shangri-La speech, IPOI pillars, partners

accepted.s: The Shangri-La Dialogue is organised by which institution and has been held in Singapore since which year?
accepted.x: The Shangri-La Dialogue is run by the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS), based in London, and has been held in Singapore since 2002.
accepted.tq: Match the forum with its organising institution and established venue timeline.
accepted.sec: Indo-Pacific vision - Shangri-La speech, IPOI pillars, partners

accepted.s: At the 2026 Shangri-La Dialogue, the United States described India as a:
accepted.x: At the 2026 edition, the United States called India a “critical anchor.”
accepted.tq: Recall the precise diplomatic description rather than substituting a stronger formal alliance term.
accepted.sec: Indo-Pacific vision - Shangri-La speech, IPOI pillars, partners

accepted.s: Which change was associated with the United States in 2026 in the Indo-Pacific security context?
o: PACOM was merged with NATO command.
The United States abolished its Pacific command.
PACOM was renamed INDOPACOM for the first time.
accepted.x: The United States reverted the name INDOPACOM to PACOM in 2026.
accepted.tq: Track the direction of the institutional name change and reject the reversed formulation.
accepted.sec: Indo-Pacific vision - Shangri-La speech, IPOI pillars, partners

accepted.s: The Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) was proposed by Prime Minister Modi at the:
o: Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore in June 2018
14th East Asia Summit in Bangkok in November 2019
First India-Central Asia Summit in January 2022
accepted.x: The IPOI was proposed at the 14th East Asia Summit held in Bangkok in November 2019.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the IPOI launch forum from the earlier Shangri-La speech.
accepted.sec: Indo-Pacific vision - Shangri-La speech, IPOI pillars, partners

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative:
1. It is open and non-treaty in character.
2. It builds on the SAGAR vision.
3. It has seven pillars.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The IPOI is open and non-treaty, builds on SAGAR, and consists of seven pillars.
accepted.tq: Test the initiative's institutional character, conceptual basis and numerical structure together.
accepted.sec: Indo-Pacific vision - Shangri-La speech, IPOI pillars, partners

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the pillars of the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative?
accepted.x: The seven IPOI pillars include Maritime Security, Maritime Ecology, Maritime Resources, Capacity Building and Resource Sharing, Disaster Risk Reduction and Management, Science, Technology and Academic Cooperation, and Trade, Connectivity and Maritime Transport. Nuclear Disarmament Verification is not one of them.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated sector among the formally listed seven pillars.
accepted.sec: Indo-Pacific vision - Shangri-La speech, IPOI pillars, partners

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (IPOI pillar)
a. Maritime Security
b. Maritime Ecology
c. Capacity Building and Resource Sharing
d. Disaster Risk Reduction and Management

List-II
 i. Environmental dimension
 ii. Safety and security at sea
 iii. Development of capabilities and sharing of resources
 iv. Management of maritime disasters
accepted.x: Maritime Security corresponds to safety and security at sea; Maritime Ecology to the environmental dimension; Capacity Building and Resource Sharing to capabilities and resource sharing; and Disaster Risk Reduction and Management to maritime disasters.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure semantic pair and eliminate codes that reverse the pillar meanings.
accepted.sec: Indo-Pacific vision - Shangri-La speech, IPOI pillars, partners

accepted.s: Which of the following countries joined the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative in January 2026?
accepted.x: Spain joined the IPOI in January 2026.
accepted.tq: Identify the new partner while distinguishing it from other European countries.
accepted.sec: Indo-Pacific vision - Shangri-La speech, IPOI pillars, partners

accepted.s: The year 2026 was designated as the India-Spain Dual Year of:
accepted.x: 2026 was designated the India-Spain Dual Year of Culture, Tourism and Artificial Intelligence.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact three-sector theme associated with the bilateral designation.
accepted.sec: Indo-Pacific vision - Shangri-La speech, IPOI pillars, partners

accepted.s: Which development occurred during the 2026 Prime Ministerial visits to Australia and New Zealand?
o: A new India-Australia Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation
The launch of the I2U2 grouping
The signing of the first India-New Zealand customs union
India's withdrawal from the Indo-Pacific framework
accepted.x: During the 2026 visits to Australia and New Zealand, a new India-Australia Joint Declaration on Defence and Security Cooperation was noted.
accepted.tq: Associate the diplomatic document with the correct country relationship and policy area.
accepted.sec: Indo-Pacific vision - Shangri-La speech, IPOI pillars, partners
